st.headline: Chinese EV maker NIO inks battery-swopping deal with Geely, open to other peers joining
st.teaser: Under the deal, Geely Holding Group will acquire a 30% stake in NIO Power.
fullText: Chinese electric vehicle maker NIO said on Sept 28 it had signed a deal with Zhejiang Geely Holding Group on their battery-swopping and charging businesses, in a bid to jointly expand and improve their charging networks.
Under the deal, Geely Holding Group will acquire a 30% stake in NIO Power, NIO’s battery-swopping and charging unit, NIO said in a statement.
For the purchase, Geely will contribute its 100% equity in its battery-swopping subsidiary Yiyi Power, plus 640 million yuan (S$121 million) in cash.
That transaction values NIO Power at about 16 billion yuan, according to NIO.

Chinese electric vehicle (EV) makers have been stepping up their battle for technological supremacy in ultra-fast charging, with Nio developing more than 4,000 battery-swop stations where a full battery replacement takes about three minutes, while Geely Auto, a flagship affiliate of Geely Holding Group, unveiled a four-minute charging technology last week.

NIO Power aims to have 10,000 battery swop stations in operation by 2030, with annual electricity demand expected to exceed 10 billion kWh, while Geely plans to expand its network to more than 22,000 charging stations by the end of 2027.
In an industry-wide race over fast EV charging, their rival BYD has been building tens of thousands of flash-charging stations.
Following the announcement, shares in NIO rose 3.2%, recovering from losses in the two previous sessions.

The companies touted their partnership as a new model in China’s car industry to build a denser and more reliable charging network to ease anxiety for EV drivers, leaving the door open for other peers to join.
The two companies will co-develop unified swopping standards and vehicle models, NIO said.
“The collaboration between NIO and Geely in charging and battery swopping is open to the broader industry. We welcome and look forward to more industry peers joining us,” NIO CEO William Li said.
As part of the deal, NIO will acquire a 10% equity stake in Geely’s smart charging subsidiary, Haohan Energy. REUTERS

cna.headline: England's Tuchel says calls for rotation are 'madness'
cna.teaser: England's Tuchel says calls for rotation are 'madness'
fullText: Sept 28 : England's players and the clubs they play for should not be allowed to pick and choose which games they feature in during the international break, manager Thomas Tuchel said.
England will play four Nations League matches during the extended international window. Tuchel's side lost to World Cup champions Spain on Saturday in the first of those games.

They next visit the Czech Republic on Tuesday and Croatia on Saturday, before playing the Czechs again at home on October 6, with the packed schedule leading to calls for some players who had short summer breaks due to the World Cup to be rested.
Asked if any club managers had reached out to him, Tuchel told reporters: "I don't take calls from Premier League managers. I never called any national team coach (when he was in club football).

"We want to win the next match... An ideal scenario would be to go again and go again and go again. With six or seven players minimum that start again – to put the responsibility on them and for them to feel the trust."
Tuchel said his team would go all out against the Czech Republic in Tuesday's match at the Fortuna Arena in Prague, adding: "We need to be proactive.
"There is no room for managing (the players) or an economic style. It's how the team want to play, how we want to play, so let's go."
A single handpicked story that we think you shouldn't miss. Just one a day.

listening.title: Singapore Steps Up Green Transition Efforts
listening.transcript: Singapore is step-by-step ramping up its efforts to meet its net-zero emission targets by 2050. During the recent budget announcement, the government confirmed a progressive hike in the carbon tax to compel local corporations to adopt cleaner energy. Analysts believe this move will nudge multinational companies to anchor their green projects in the city-state.

economistArticle.title: The battle between India’s stock exchanges is heating up again
paras: For years, India’s equity landscape was a tale of comfortable coexistence. The venerable Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), founded in 1875 as Asia’s oldest, possessed history, while its younger rival, the National Stock Exchange (NSE), held the crown for technology and trading volumes. Yet this cosy duopoly is now giving way to fierce combat as BSE tries to reclaim its lost glory.

The battleground is primarily the highly lucrative derivatives market. Historically, the NSE enjoyed a near-monopoly in equity derivatives, leaving BSE with negligible market share. However, under the leadership of a new chief executive, Sundararaman Ramamurthy, BSE has aggressively overhauled its product offerings, slashing transaction fees and restructuring its weekly options contracts to directly challenge the NSE’s dominance.

The results of this tactical offensive have been swift and striking. BSE’s market share in equity derivatives has surged from practically zero to over fifteen percent within a short span. This resurgence has not only forced NSE to reconsider its pricing strategy but has also sparked concerns about market stability, as retail participation in highly speculative derivative contracts reaches fever pitch.

Regulatory bodies are watching the skirmish with mounting anxiety. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has repeatedly warned of the systemic risks associated with retail investors piling into options. There is a delicate balance to strike; while competition breeds efficiency and lowers costs for traders, a price war that encourages excessive speculation could end in tears.

Looking ahead, the NSE cannot afford to rest on its laurels. It is currently preparing for an initial public offering (IPO) that has been delayed for years due to legacy regulatory issues. To secure a premium valuation, the NSE must prove it can fend off BSE's encroachment on its turf, ensuring that India’s financial architecture remains both competitive and safe.
economistArticle.cn:
多年来，印度的股市格局一直是一个安逸共存的故事。成立于1875年、作为亚洲最古老交易所的孟买证券交易所（BSE）拥有悠久的历史，而其年轻的竞争对手国家证券交易所（NSE）则在技术和交易量上夺得桂冠。然而，随着BSE试图重夺昔日荣光，这种舒适的双头垄断如今正演变为一场激烈的战斗。

战场主要集中在利润极其丰厚的衍生品市场上。历史上，NSE在股票衍生品领域享有近乎垄断的地位，给BSE留下的市场份额微乎其微。然而，在新任首席执行官桑达拉拉曼·拉玛穆尔蒂的领导下，BSE积极重组其产品线，大幅削减交易费用并重构每周选择权合约，直接向NSE的霸主地位发起挑战。

这一战术性攻势的结果既迅速又惊人。在极短的时间内，BSE在股票衍生品领域的市场份额已从几乎为零飙升至15%以上。这一复苏不仅迫使NSE重新审视其定价策略，也引发了人们对市场稳定性的担忧，因为散户参与高度投机性衍生品合约的热情已达到了白热化的程度。

监管机构正怀着日益加剧的焦虑注视着这场小规模冲突。印度证券交易委员会（SEBI）已多次警告散户投资者涌入期权交易带来的系统性风险。这里需要取得一种微妙的平衡：虽然竞争能提高效率并降低交易者的成本，但一场鼓励过度投机的价格战最终可能会以悲剧收场。

展望未来，NSE无法再固步自封。由于历史遗留的监管问题，它目前正准备推迟多年的首次公开募股（IPO）。为了确保获得溢价估值，NSE必须证明其有能力抵御BSE对其领地的蚕食，确保印度的金融体系既保持竞争力又安全稳健。

gems.s: For years, India’s equity landscape was a tale of comfortable coexistence.
gems.why: This opening sentence uses literary personification and metaphor ('a tale of comfortable coexistence') to contrast with the aggressive market warfare that follows, engaging the reader immediately. 作者使用了文学化的拟人和比喻手法（“安逸共存的故事”）来与随后紧烈、残酷的商业竞争形成鲜明对比，瞬间吸引了读者的阅读兴趣。

gems.s: To secure a premium valuation, the NSE must prove it can fend off BSE's encroachment on its turf.
gems.why: The author uses vivid financial terminology ('premium valuation') coupled with action-oriented metaphors ('fend off' and 'encroachment on its turf') to describe defensive corporate strategy dynamically. 作者将专业财经术语（“溢价估值”）与极具动感的比喻（“击退对手对领地的蚕食”）相结合，生动形象地描述了公司防御性的战略举措。
